clinician.trajectory_summary: A 74-year-old male presented in 2005 with a one-year history of pruritic cutaneous lesions on his left lower extremity, with physical examination revealing an erythematous plaque and cord-like nodular lesions on the left thigh and leg. Initial workup in 2005 included culture, histopathology, and mycological examinations, but the patient was subsequently lost to follow-up. The patient re-presented in 2017 with progression of disease, now manifesting as ulcers with perilesional induration, erythema, and desquamation on the left leg, along with cord-like, firm, brown nodules along the medial aspect of the left thigh and leg. Routine laboratory studies in 2017 were unremarkable. Skin biopsy from the 2017 presentation demonstrated hyperkeratosis, epidermal acanthosis, diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, giant cells, hemosiderin-laden histiocytes, and increased vascularity in the papillary dermis, with round structures present in the reticular dermis. Grocott's methenamine silver stain revealed numerous round yeasts with thick double walls, occurring singly or in chains connected by tubular projections—characteristic morphology of Lacazia loboi. The final pathology report diagnosis was lobomycosis.
